label: Scenario catalog for the /flow page. Each tape is a recorded ERCOT window; overlays are labeled.

scenarios.name: Winter Storm Heather
scenarios.summary: Recorded NP3-233-CD outage postings and four-zone NP6-905-CD prices. The storm rule reads HIGH only after the 13:03 posting.
scenarios.label: recorded ERCOT; target synthetic

scenarios.name: Heather: cheap afternoon, $1,165 evening
scenarios.summary: Winter Storm Heather, day after the HIGH posting. LZ_HOUSTON dips near $21 from 14:30 to 16:30, then spikes to $1,165 around 18:15. The storm rule reads LOW, so the fleet charges, then sells.
scenarios.label: recorded ERCOT; target synthetic:price-shaped

scenarios.name: Heather thaw: sell the morning, charge at noon
scenarios.summary: Last storm day. LZ_HOUSTON is $70 to $87 around 07:00, then falls to $6 by 15:00. The fleet sells into the morning and charges through the cheap afternoon.
scenarios.label: recorded ERCOT; target synthetic:price-shaped

scenarios.name: Calm day: charge at noon, sell at the peak
scenarios.summary: A normal late-summer day. LZ_NORTH sits under $25 until about 12:45 (low $12), then climbs to $225 around 19:30. Charge first, then sell.
scenarios.label: recorded ERCOT; target synthetic:price-shaped

scenarios.name: Storm rule HIGH: the 60% floor
scenarios.summary: The postings from 04:00 to 12:00 rate HIGH (North outages over the +15% margin), so every zone keeps 60%. The 13:00 posting reads LOW and the floor drops back to 30%. Baseline is the same month (in sample).
scenarios.label: recorded ERCOT; target synthetic:price-shaped

scenarios.name: Price spike: LZ_NORTH over $1,000
scenarios.summary: The same day, after the storm rule reads LOW again. LZ_NORTH goes from $225 to $498 at 18:00 and passes $1,000 around 19:45. The price-shaped ask rises to its 1.0 MW cap and the fleet sells until it reaches its floor.
scenarios.label: recorded ERCOT; target synthetic:price-shaped

scenarios.name: Storm rule turns HIGH mid-peak
scenarios.summary: The fleet sells into a $90 to $213 evening. The 21:00 posting rates HIGH, so the floor rises to 60% while prices are still high. The 02:00 posting reads LOW again.
scenarios.label: recorded ERCOT; target synthetic:price-shaped

scenarios.name: Feed failure: postings withheld
scenarios.summary: A cheap day with a $55 to $76 evening. From 18:00 to 21:00 the builder withholds the outage postings (overlay), so the rule fails safe: signal_unavailable and a 60% floor. Only charge above 60% can be sold until the postings return.
scenarios.label: recorded ERCOT; target synthetic:price-shaped; overlays (hand-placed, not archive): postings withheld 18:00-21:00 (feed failure)

scenarios.name: Faults at the peak: lossy network, crashes, misreports
scenarios.summary: LZ_NORTH is cheap until noon, then spikes to $484 around 20:00. During the peak the builder adds simulated faults (overlays): a lossy network, five crashed homes, two misreporting homes. Floors still hold.
scenarios.label: recorded ERCOT; target synthetic:price-shaped; overlays (hand-placed, not archive): lossy network 19:00-20:30, 5 homes crash 19:30, 2 homes misreport 20:00-20:30, crashed homes back 21:00

scenarios.name: Operator HOLD through the peak
scenarios.summary: LZ_NORTH runs $105 to $380 from 16:30 and peaks near $720 around 18:15. An operator HOLD (overlay) stops all dispatch from 16:45 to 18:15, so the charge is still there when the rules resume on AUTO at the peak.
scenarios.label: recorded ERCOT; target synthetic:price-shaped; overlays (hand-placed, not archive): operator HOLD 16:45-18:15, AUTO from 18:15

scenarios.name: Hurricane Beryl landfall
scenarios.summary: Beryl came ashore early on July 8. Houston load fell away and LZ_HOUSTON went negative from about 08:00 to 13:30. Prices stay under $25 all window, so the fleet charges to full; the storm rule never read HIGH. The operator can mark a zone's grid down (overlay) to show batteries carrying homes.
scenarios.label: recorded ERCOT; target synthetic:price-shaped
